newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Highlights of Tuesday's Commission briefing. [CORRECTED 13:05 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Highlights of Tuesday's Commission briefing. [CORRECTED 13:05 GMT]

text.p: Following are highlights of the midday briefing by the European Commission on Tuesday:
Spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida said Commission President Jacques Santer would attend the fifth annual summit between EU and Japan on October 1 to 4 (corrects dates from October 3 and 4).

Vale de Almeida said the agenda would include political and commercial discussions. He said political dialogue would focus on EU-Japan cooperation in ex-Yougoslavia, situation in Korea and the Middle-East and commercial dialog would focus on the World Trade Organisation (WTO) ministerial in Singapore and the Japanese deregulation programme.

Spokesman Peter Guilford said the EU would take part in a Quad meeting with United States, Japan and Canada on Saturday in Seattle. He said the objective was to obtain a position as unified as possible between the four participants on issues to be discussed during the WTO meeting in Singapore. Discussion would focus on implementation as well as on new measures to be taken, he said.

Guilford also said that an informal meeting was taking place to discuss possible Information Technology Agreement (ITA) with Japan and the United States. He added that though Europeans were in favor of an ITA, it would be difficult before the EU could be included in the global semi-conductor council between Japan and the United States.
The Commission released the following documents:
- IP/96/849: EU/Yemen: Seventh Joint Co-operate Commitee meeting.
- IP/96/850: An opportunity for European business managers to travel to Japan.
- IP/96/851: Commission clears the non-military aspects of a joint venture between British Aerospace and Lagardere.
- Speech/96/922: Address by Commissioner Neil Kinnock to the Irish Belgian Business Association on "The transport challenge - European perspectives"
- Eurostat, News release 59/96: Little change in EU industrial production.
